items.title: Beyond utility: Relational conflicts in human–AI relationships
items.abstract: Human–AI relationships are increasingly marked by emotional depth, intimacy, and social expectations. While interpersonal conflicts are common in human–human relationships, we know little about conflicts in human–AI relationships. Drawing on Social Penetration Theory, this paper examines conflicts between humans and social AIs, such as Replika Character.ai and ChatGPT. We conducted a questionnaire study with 95 participants in close, friendship-like, or romantic relationships with social AI. Participants described at least one conflict episode, yielding 161 conflicts in total. Thematic analysis of open-ended responses identified conflict topics, triggers, and emotional reactions, revealing that conflicts extend beyond technical issues and arise across emotional, relational, opinion-based, role-play, and task-oriented interactions. Three main classes of conflict triggers emerged: (1) relational triggers, including relational–emotional disconnect, breaches of trust, jealousy, boundary violations, or perceived hostility; (2) technical or functional triggers, including communication failures, unhelpful output, or external disruptions; and (3) value or opinion-based triggers. Conflicts varied in duration, some brief, others lasting hours or days. Participants reported experiencing emotions such as anger, frustration, sadness, and confusion, and perceiving social AI’s emotions, including jealousy, sadness, and defensiveness. Crucially, social AI responses appeared to shape conflict trajectories: apologetic or empathic replies were reported to de-escalate tension, whereas dismissive or accusatory responses intensified it. This study advances our understanding of how conflicts with social AI emerge, presenting implications for theory and the ethical design of technologies involved in human–AI relationships.

items.title: Does Mobile Technology Integration Enhance Complaint Resolution Efficiency and Equity? An Empirical Study of How an Omnichannel Approach Affects Speed of Resolution of Government Service Requests
items.abstract: This paper examines how integrating mobile touchpoints with existing service channels affects the efficiency and equity of nonemergency complaint resolution for cities. In 2015, Boston integrated its existing citizen app with its phone and website services into a single unified “311” service, where complaints would be handled consistently regardless of submission channel. This was among the first efforts in the United States to bring an omnichannel approach to public services. We document that this change had an unexpected effect. Before integration, the app delivered more equitable service across higher- and lower-income neighborhoods than other channels. After integration, because the app made it easier to submit a broader range of complaints, it was increasingly used in requests on enforcing city codes against other residents. The mobile app allowed quicker resolution of enforcement complaints, especially in richer areas with signs of gentrification. The pattern appears to be driven by the economics of density: residents in wealthier neighborhoods are more likely to submit multiple enforcement requests simultaneously. Complaints requiring citations were processed more quickly when related requests came from geographically concentrated areas rather than dispersed locations.

items.title: EE-Profile: Structuring Life Narratives into Event-Enhanced Profile for Elder Care
items.abstract: Life narratives can support person-centered care in long-term care, but existing representations are often either too long to scan quickly or too brief to provide useful context during time-pressured care. We present Event-Enhanced Profile (EE-Profile), a two-level representation that combines concise facet entities for rapid scanning with event timelines for contextual access during routine care workflows. Events are schema-structured tuples with provenance links to the original narratives. We also design a large language model pipeline that transforms narrative transcripts into facet entities and event tuples. In four studies with 8 older adults and 31 care-team participants recruited from two nursing homes and two hospital-based geriatric care units in two Chinese cities, EE-Profile improved information-retrieval efficiency and reduced perceived workload versus raw narratives in controlled task settings. Participants reported high usability and greater readiness to initiate personalized conversations. Source-linked event timelines show promise for making life narratives usable in time-pressured care.

items.title: Effects of Human Centered AI Supported Instruction on EFL Listening With Adaptive Feedback Gamified Engagement and Motivational Scaffolding
items.abstract: Abstract Listening comprehension remains one of the most cognitively demanding yet comparatively underemphasized components of English as a Foreign Language (EFL) instruction, particularly in adolescent classrooms. Addressing this gap, the present mixed-methods study investigated the effects of AI-supported instruction on learners’ listening comprehension, engagement, and motivation. Two instructional conditions were implemented under controlled classroom settings: a gamified AI-driven personalized learning system (Duolingo) incorporating progression tracking and structured feedback, and a non-gamified conversational AI platform (Replika) designed for personalized dialogue practice without game-based reward mechanisms such as points or badges. The study was conceptually informed by Schema Theory, Self-Regulation Theory, Dynamic Assessment within Sociocultural Theory, and Gamification Theory, which were synthesized into two integrative frameworks—the AI-Enhanced Language Learning Matrix (AELLM) and the Intelligent Learning Environment Design (ILED). Based on the mixed-methods findings, Tajik’s Scaffolded Motivator Model (T-SMM) was proposed as an explanatory model of motivational scaffolding in AI-mediated listening instruction. Participants included 53 Iranian high school learners (aged 14–15) who completed a 12-week instructional program comprising 24 sessions. Quantitative results indicated significant improvements in listening proficiency and self-efficacy in the gamified condition, while qualitative findings revealed enhanced engagement and perceived instructional support. The findings suggest that structured feedback and gamified scaffolding may support sustained participation and deeper cognitive engagement. These results contribute to the design and evaluation of AI-supported EFL listening environments and offer practical implications for technology-enhanced language instruction.
